answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III and place face down; shuffle 9 II and deal 5 on top; shuffle 3 I and deal 1 on top, yielding 10 cards in I/II/III order. Return unused conflicts to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: “Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck … Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: Four-player: score starts at 1; three-player: 0. Both start with 2 Agents on Leader and third (Swordmaster) aside, 3 troops in garrison plus 9 in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: Score marker on 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader; three troops in garrison and nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, and after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns, so you cannot Agent-turn later that round. Resolve only Reveal boxes of cards remaining in hand, not cards used on Agent turns; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Reveal turns are optional before exhausting Agents; “Once you’ve taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped”; Reveal effects of just-revealed cards only; Clean Up all cards.

answers.answer: No. Entry must be paid immediately before effects of the space or played card; effects gained after placement cannot pay that entry. One card sends one Agent using one icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Agent Turn: “You choose only one Agent icon; one card can’t send multiple Agents”; entry before resolving effects; no Agent icon means Reveal only.

answers.answer: At a Combat space deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 of the 4 already in your garrison: up to 5. At a non-Combat space recruited troops remain in the garrison. Recruit from your supply; if empty, you cannot recruit until troops return.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: any/all units recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison at Combat spaces; cube recruits from supply.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets the card send an Agent to a space connected to one of your Spy posts without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate recalls a connected Spy to bypass another player's Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after placing your Agent, before space/card effects, to draw a card. The same Spy cannot pay for both; two different Spies may pay Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ Spies: Spy Agent icon; Infiltrate; Gather Intelligence timing; two Spies for different effects, never same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11 (2 troops × 2 + 1 sandworm × 3 + 4 swords). If your last unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, worm 3, sword 1; if last unit removed strength 0. Combat Intrigue: only players with at least one unit in Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes; passing once does not bar you from playing later. The window closes after all involved players pass consecutively. After rewards troops return to supply (not garrison), Combat markers reset to 0, and worms return to bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; resolve after all pass consecutively; cleanup instructions.

answers.answer: In both ties for first, each tied player receives the second reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With four players, the remaining players compete for third if exactly two tie first; with three players there are no other rewards. A player at 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first receive second reward, no winner/card; different handling at 3 or fewer versus 4 players. Resolve Combat: 0 strength gets no reward.

answers.answer: One or more worms doubles rewards once; two worms do not quadruple. Control and battle-icon matches do not double. For an optional reward of 3 spice for 1 VP, pay 3 spice for the first and may pay 3 more for a second, up to 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: “one or more”; control and battle icons excluded; optional cost may be paid a second time, example 3 or 6 spice.

answers.answer: When you win and take a Conflict card, check for a same-icon face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply; matching is mandatory, flip both face down for 1 VP. During Endgame the wild icon may match any one of the three icons; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: checked when winning/taking card; face-up Conflict or Objective; must match; wild usable during Endgame.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence gain 1 VP, lost below 2 and regained on returning to 2. At 4 gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; first to 4 also takes Alliance and 1 VP tied to holding it. Merely tying the Alliance holder does not steal it; an opponent must rise higher. Alliance VP transfers with token.
answers.evidence: Scoring, Faction Influence: 2 VP; 4 track bonus and Alliance token; tying does not steal; token VP follows holder.

answers.answer: Spend Persuasion during Reveal before, between, or after Reveal effects. Pool sources to buy one card or split one source among purchases. Row replacements are immediately available if affordable. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: timing, pool/split, Row remains five, acquire replacement, destination is discard.

answers.answer: Maker spaces accrue 1 bonus spice each Makers phase when Agent-free; visiting gains all accumulated bonus spice even if choosing worms. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are retained, not spent. Wall prevents summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin until removed. Worms go directly into Conflict, never garrison.
answers.evidence: Phase Makers; Sandworms; Board Space Guide; FAQ Maker Hooks retained.

answers.answer: At Recall at round end, if anyone has 10+ VP or Conflict deck is empty, Endgame triggers. Players first may play/resolve Endgame Intrigue, then highest VP wins. Tiebreaks: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, in that order.
answers.evidence: Phase 5 Recall; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: CHOAM setup: 2 contracts face up and remaining 18 of the 20 face down in bank. Shuffle 4 extra Intrigue and 4 extra Imperium cards into their decks. Shaddam is an optional Leader. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay out; they are not part of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes; Components and Scope.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, contract icon takes one of the 2 face-up tokens into your supply and replaces it from bank face up; if all contracts taken, icon gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes by sending an Agent to Maker space and gaining shown spice total that turn; Immediate completes on taking it; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module, Taking contracts and Completing contracts.

answers.answer: No: you must hold the board-space contract when sending the Agent there, so one gained after that visit waits for a future turn. On completion announce it, gain its displayed rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: must have had contract when sent; FAQ Contract completion.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. Rival gets Ornithopter Objective; humans are dealt the other two eligible Objectives and First Player is the human whose Objective shows the marker. Order is First Player → Rival → other human. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: If destination is occupied, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card places a Spy at an empty specified post if possible, then reveal another Hagal card and continue the same Agent turn; it does not place an Agent. Ignore normal space costs/effects and use only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Place Spy cards; normal costs/effects ignored; Reshuffle.

answers.answer: For 3–4 players, shuffle Objectives after removing those marked for the wrong player count; each player draws one randomly. The Objective showing First Player marker determines first player. Shaddam is only used with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5.

answers.answer: The resource and sandworm bank is not limited; make convenient substitutions if it runs out. Troops differ: an empty personal supply means you cannot recruit until troops return there. Resource payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 6–7: recruit supply; bank resources/sandworms not limited; payments returned to bank.

answers.answer: Five phases: Round Start (reveal Conflict, then draw five cards), Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. If no Endgame at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player marker clockwise, and start next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phase descriptions; Player Reference.

answers.answer: Yes, board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence may be resolved in any order. No, entry requirements and costs must be met before effects, so Influence gained on that visit cannot qualify you to enter.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: effects may be in any order; costs/requirements before placement and effects. Board Space Guide says pay entry before effects.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect can be paid only once per turn, except sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward. Most effects are mandatory; “may,” optional arrow costs and black-X trash are optional, but direct trash instructions are mandatory. Intrigue conditions/costs must all be met to play.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If supply has none, you may first recall one of your own Spies for no effect. If placement specifies an Agent-icon connection, that type must be connected to the post or placement cannot occur.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses only another player's Agent. Recalling a Spy for Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence still requires playing a card for an Agent turn. Two different Spies may pay Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, but not two Gather Intelligence draws on one placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ Spies.

answers.answer: The controller receives a separate visit bonus when anyone (including controller) visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict places/replaces control marker. On Conflict reveal, controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Round Start.

answers.answer: Tie for second: each tied player gets the third reward; Conflict winner keeps rewards/card and no further rewards are given. Tie for third: tied players get nothing. Three tied for first in four-player play: each gets second reward, no winner/card and no other rewards.
answers.evidence: Combat ties.

answers.answer: With three players and three different positive strengths, first and second receive rewards; third receives nothing. Same in two humans plus Rival, which counts as 3-player play; Rival can receive a rank reward.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: 2 or 3 players, ordinary first/second paid; ordinary third nothing.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues are playable during your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from deck; reveal only when played; after resolution discard face up beside Intrigue Deck. If deck empties, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Intrigue cards; FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: No, ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. Secrets steals one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent with 4 or more.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Discarding and Intrigue cards; Board Space Guide, Secrets.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Ordinary trashed cards return to box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional except as a cost or when card directs trashing itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquired VP is retained if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ Victory.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effect resolves once immediately when acquiring the card. If deck is empty when drawing, shuffle discard into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost at end of Reveal and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on Reveal remain in play until Clean Up (unless trashed); Fremen Bond checks other Fremen cards in play. Two Bond cards can activate one another in either play order. They cease being in play when moved to discard at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents, not the one just sent; it can be used on another Agent turn the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to garrison. “Retreat any number” permits zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: A single free-choice effect granting two Influence must put both with one chosen Faction; it cannot split. Faction-specific effects use only the shown Faction. Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance; minimum-Influence effects require the stated Influence.
answers.evidence: Influence; Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: If holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes Alliance; if multiple, former holder chooses which. If holder falls to 3 or less and nobody at 4+, Alliance returns to board. Old holder loses its 1 VP on transfer/return.
answers.evidence: FAQ Alliance loss; Scoring Faction Influence.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, then five additional cards are drawn. Plot Intrigue with later Reveal effect stays face up until used at Reveal, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing.

answers.answer: No, tying for first is not winning, so cannot play a “when you win” Intrigue afterward. If received as reward for an outright win, it can be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops.

answers.answer: If VP and all four rulebook tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores can exceed the printed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts held for the same space with one Agent placement. Their effects are another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects; must have held contracts when sending Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion.

answers.answer: No, Shaddam does not start with set-aside Sardaukar contracts; Sardaukar Commander lets him choose such a contract instead of generally available one when taking a contract. Emperor of the Known Universe restriction starts immediately when playing Signet Ring to send Agent and lasts that turn only, not whole round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd token starts at leftmost Training track space and stays at rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side starts face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2 even when gaining multiple Influence at once. Can reach 2 again later by losing Influence then regaining; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications.

answers.answer: Accept Contract is Spice Trade; draw a card; with CHOAM take contract, otherwise gain 2 Solari (also if none remain). Dutiful Service is Emperor; gain 1 Emperor Influence and take contract with CHOAM, otherwise 2 Solari. Accept Contract has no automatic Faction Influence; Dutiful Service is a Faction space and its 1 Emperor Influence is gained once.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; intro explains Faction icons: Accept Contract no automatic Influence; Faction space 1 Influence not twice.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City, Combat, no cost; visitor recruits 1 troop and draws 1 card. Fremkit: Fremen, Combat, no cost; +1 Fremen Influence and draw 1. Research Station: City, Combat, costs 2 water; recruit 2 and draw 2.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and gives all accumulated bonus spice; choose 4 base spice or, with Hooks, summon 2 worms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and gives all bonus spice; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon 1 worm. Bonus is collected either way; Hooks retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworm Reward Doubling/Special Rules; FAQ Spies.

answers.answer: Requires 2+ Fremen. Option 1: take Maker Hooks if lacking, recruit 1 troop, gain 1 water. Option 2: gain 1 water and optionally remove Shield Wall. Removing Wall does not grant troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide, Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: Costs 5 Solari each visit; not a Combat space. First visit places Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on each Reveal for rest of game. Subsequent visits grant 2 spice, draw Intrigue, recruit 3 troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide, High Council.

answers.answer: Costs 8 Solari before anyone obtains Swordmaster, then 6. Once per player per game. Take third Agent from next to board onto Leader; available this round and thereafter. Rival gaining Swordmaster also lowers human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide, Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, costs 3 Solari, not a Combat space. May discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide, Imperial Privilege.

answers.answer: Shipping is Spice Trade, requires 2+ Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction. Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide, Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support (Landsraad, not Combat): choose pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit 2 troops, and if paid 2 gain 1 water. Spice Refinery (City, Combat): choose pay 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari, or 4 if paid 1; controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: Heighliner (Guild Combat): pay 5 spice, gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit 5 troops. Desert Tactics (Fremen Combat): pay 1 water, gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1, optionally trash card. Sardaukar (Emperor, non-Combat): pay 4 spice, gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw Intrigue, recruit 4. Only first two allow normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall (Landsraad, no cost): draw Intrigue; gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal if Agent remains there. Espionage (Bene Gesserit, cost 1 spice): +1 BG Influence, draw card, place Spy. Deliver Supplies (Guild, no cost): +1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; may play even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If still unacquired by end of your next Reveal, remove it from game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate.

answers.answer: Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms; 3 troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply; 2 Agents in supply plus Swordmaster aside; 3 Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat marker 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining 2P Reshuffle card. Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup; Rival can win paragraph.

answers.answer: When Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water together reach its printed Swordmaster value, spend that many: Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water. Keep leftovers; new Agent usable this round immediately.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, spend sets of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP per such set. No, mixed seven resources do not make VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Resources and Swordmaster: exact individual resource sets.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, Rival uses the Faction with least Influence; break ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains VP at 2 and Alliance VP like a human, but does not get the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in its card’s priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: “When choosing Influence, use the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon”; gains/losses Influence VP and Alliances like human, no resource bonus at 4.

answers.answer: No. With a two-destination Hagal card select only the destination matching current conditions; if occupied reveal another card, do not use other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Agent turns.

answers.answer: Yes, at each Combat space Rival deploys up to 2 available garrison troops even if card recruited none. Newly recruited at a noncombat space go to garrison. A missing 2+ Influence bonus does not prevent Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Agent turns.

answers.answer: Unless post type specified, place Spy at first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four occupied ignore placement. Placing third/final supply Spy recalls its other two and triggers Scheme. Rival never recalls Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If Scheme recruited troops before Agent placement and Rival then visits Combat space same turn, deploy those troops too. If Place Spy has no legal post, ignore placement but reveal another Hagal card because it did not send Agent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Place Spy cards; Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: Rival always collects all bonus spice at visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin/Deep Desert, with Hooks and Conflict permitting worms, summon 1 or 2 respectively instead of base spice; without Hooks or if protected, take base spice (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4). Hooks are not spent. Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces paragraph: always gets bonus spice; with Hooks and unprotected summons; if none summoned take base spice; Hagal Hooks icon takes token if needed.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal a Hagal card in turn order; add only its bottom swords as strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have normal Combat Intrigue window. Unit-free Rival gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: Rival gets normal placement rewards, doubles with one or more worms, and wins cards/battle-icon VP normally; it gains control and defensive troop bonuses. It always takes optional Conflict VP if able to pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total Combat strength and announce it; set marker at any point during resolving, updating as needed. Above 20 flip marker to +20 side and start again at beginning of track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn; Strength.

answers.answer: Leader's Signet ability activates when Signet Ring is played on one of your Agent turns, not merely revealed. Card text can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3; Overview.

answers.answer: Recall Spy icon on card returns one of your Spies from an observation post to supply, usually as cost for a powerful effect. It does not by itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate Spy recalls without card.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: Trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Ordinary discard is from your hand and cannot be Intrigue unless specified; discard does not trash.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: Doubling a reward that grants one free-choice Influence allows two gains, choosing the same or different Factions. A single effect granting two free-choice Influence must choose one Faction for both.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling; Influence.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring effect printed on the Rival card as a Hagal effect; it does not need a human Signet Ring card or Reveal turn. Rival follows its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow printed Signet Ring abilities; apply revealed Hagal effects including Signet Ring.

answers.answer: If Rival lacks Hooks, Maker Hooks icon takes them; if it already has them it has no additional effect. Shield Wall removal removes it if present; if already gone, nothing changes. Hooks are retained when summoning.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules says apply Maker Hooks icons; Sandworms; FAQ Spies says Hooks retained.

answers.answer: Secrets: Bene Gesserit icon, no cost, not a Combat space. Gain 1 BG Influence and draw an Intrigue from deck; each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide, Secrets.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin is Spice Trade, no entry cost, Combat space. Visitor gains 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice; controller separately gains 1 spice, including if visitor and controller are same player (so that player gains both).
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide, Imperial Basin; controlled locations resolve visitor and controller effects even when same player.

answers.answer: Reveal new Conflict from top and place face up next to deck on top of any unclaimed Conflict cards from earlier rounds. Then each player draws five cards. Thus reveal precedes hands, and prior unclaimed conflicts remain beneath it.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: reveal new Conflict and place on top of previous round cards, then players draw five.

answers.answer: Each human's four cubes start on bottom spaces of four Influence tracks; four Alliance tokens begin on marked areas of those tracks, so nobody starts holding one. Shield Wall token starts in marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6.

answers.answer: First Player starts, then clockwise; each takes one Agent or Reveal turn. After Revealing, that player's turns are skipped; phase ends once all players Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, start First Player and proceed clockwise; each eligible player may play any number or pass. Window closes after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 Player Turns; Phase 3 Combat.

answers.answer: Three steps: Reveal Cards; Resolve Reveal Effects; Clean Up. Effects may be resolved in any order, not necessarily card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn.

answers.answer: Each human 10-card starter deck is shuffled face down in supply left of Leader. Intrigue deck is shuffled face down. Imperium deck shuffled face down and deal 5 face up to Row. Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow each form separate Reserve stacks. Combat marker starts 0; 3 Spies and Councilor in supply; Control markers are in supply. Without CHOAM omit CHOAM-marked cards before shuffle.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4, 6; Initial card states.

answers.answer: During Reveal, spend Persuasion on any five Imperium Row cards or Reserve cards Prepare the Way/The Spice Must Flow; cost at top right. These are normal Reveal-turn acquisitions.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Ordinary human Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even if legal; may decline. Shield Wall detonation icon may remove Wall; destruction is optional. Once removed it stays gone and cannot return.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies; Shield Wall.

answers.answer: Played card must have matching Agent icon for destination, or its Spy Agent icon with Spy at connected post. A connected Spy alone doesn't provide Shipping access to card with only City icon. If card has Spy Agent icon, it can send Agent to any connected space without recalling Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: Yes. During own Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue, and resources it grants before Agent placement can pay entry. Resources from the Agent card or destination are gained only after placement and cannot pay that same entry.
answers.evidence: Phase 2, Plot Intrigue and Agent Turn entry-cost timing.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play after both humans Revealed, skip them but continue Rival Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. Combat begins only when both humans Revealed and Rival used all Agents. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Phase 2, two-player turn rule.

answers.answer:
| Space | Access icon | Combat? |
| Accept Contract | Spice Trade | No |
| Arrakeen | City | Yes |
| Assembly Hall | Landsraad | No |
| Deep Desert | Spice Trade | Yes |
| Deliver Supplies | Spacing Guild | No |
| Desert Tactics | Fremen | Yes |
| Dutiful Service | Emperor | No |
| Espionage | Bene Gesserit | No |
| Fremkit | Fremen | Yes |
| Gather Support | Landsraad | No |
| Hagga Basin | Spice Trade | Yes |
| Heighliner | Spacing Guild | Yes |
| High Council | Landsraad | No |
| Imperial Basin | Spice Trade | Yes |
| Imperial Privilege | Landsraad | No |
| Research Station | City | Yes |
| Sardaukar | Emperor | No |

| Shipping | Spice Trade | No |
| Sietch Tabr | City | Yes |
| Spice Refinery | City | Yes |
| Swordmaster | Landsraad | No | Supported.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists 22 standard spaces with access icons and Combat markings.

answers.answer: At Round Start, when a Conflict is revealed for a location already controlled, controller may deploy 1 troop directly from supply to Conflict, with no Agent visit. It is optional. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 defensive bonus; Phase 3 Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader onto a matching unoccupied space. Resolve only the Agent box, not Reveal box. Cards already in play or discard cannot be reused, and an Agent already on board cannot simply be moved.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn.

answers.answer: Restriction applies immediately when playing Signet Ring to send Agent, so he cannot delay it by resolving board-space effects first. Shaddam rule clarifies normal effect-order flexibility cannot postpone restriction.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications, Shaddam.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths and no worms, first, second and third receive printed rewards; fourth gets none. Highest-strength winner takes Conflict card.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat, four-player ranks.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select at random; either is permitted.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: “choose, or select at random.”

answers.answer: Ordinary draw effects draw from your own deck. If empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue; you cannot choose a card directly from discard pile.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Drawing cards.
